about: Owner decision list D4 of the audit-fix spec (T3 item 2): every result that leaves `generatable` against dbc5eeb or 7345490f needs an owner decision. Proposals from benchmarks/t3/evidence.md; owner_decision stays null until the owner decides, and the executor never fills it. benchmarks/t3/tools/acceptance_compare.py separates a described transition (an entry matches) from an approved one (decision_format below) and lists every pending row with its exact key in the `d4_pending_rows` of its JSON report. This revision is bound to the candidate 9a5baf3e (the T3 acceptance run of 2026-10-13): every entry was re-checked against that candidate's reports, its triage and the fresh replays of 2026-10-13 (R11-A2, R11-C2/B2), not carried over from the 6e62e0d1 revision; the earlier text of substantially changed entries is kept under `previous`

decision_format.owner_decision: null (pending) or {"decision": "accept" | "reject", "candidate_library_sha256": <64 hex of the accepted candidate>, "rows": [{"corpus", "file", "tokenizer", "outcome"}], "by": <name>, "date": <YYYY-MM-DD>, "note": <text>}
decision_format.approval: a transition row is approved only when its entry has decision accept, the decision names the candidate's library sha256 (the same hash in both corpora), and `rows` lists the row with the exact corpus, file, tokenizer and candidate outcome; a wildcard is never a row. An entry with requires_triage_class needs, in addition, that row's class in the T2c triage of the same candidate (benchmarks/triage_semantic.py --out-json) with every invalid document present and checked.
decision_format.candidate: candidate_library_sha256 above names the candidate the proposals were written for; a comparison with another candidate reports every decision as not applicable

The candidate needs 7.1 % more time than its own source built for the host CPU (median over results at the deciding check, range 1.046-1.100; pre-registered heuristic threshold 4.5 %, the round-to-round noise; not a confidence interval; 25/25 results above 1), the code against 50cbd80e is 1.027. Leading hypothesis by the rule: the release CPU target (-Dcpu=baseline) as the leading hypothesis for the target ratio. Limits: Pre-registered reading rule, kept as a diagnostic heuristic: target = M(cand)/M(native) and code = M(native)/M(50cbd80e) medians against the threshold max(2 %, noise). The threshold is not a confidence interval; a median inside it does not prove equivalence, one outside it does not prove a cause, and the rule cannot attribute the residual to run conditions - it only says the measured ratio difference is not separable from the round-to-round noise by this design. Same document = equal documents; token paths and masks were not recorded. The release recipe builds with -Dcpu=baseline (the release workflow did so already at dbc5eeb: .github/workflows/release.yml); the lines' libraries were host builds. In the recorded runs the time-limited passes 2-20 of 6e62e0d1 and 9a5baf3e reach the same steps (median ratio ~1; compatible with, not proof of, equal speed), and the pass-1 flips between the two runs go both ways: four rows completed on 9a5baf3e that recorded a limit on 6e62e0d1 (D4-15, D4-16, D4-24, D4-33, now retired), and the two GPT-2 rows recorded a limit that completed on 6e62e0d1 and in the line (D4-39, D4-40). Hypothesis (stated as such): the differing recorded pass-1 outcomes follow the run's conditions at the 10 s check; the cause of the flips is not established beyond this. In the recorded runs the time-limited passes 2-20 of the two candidates reach the same steps (same seeds; median step ratio 1.000 over 19 passes; compatible with, but not proof of, equal speed). The deterministic pass-1 document is the same on every library, so a difference in the document is excluded; a small timing difference between the two candidates is not excluded by these data. Hypothesis (stated as such): the differing recorded pass-1 outcomes follow the run's conditions at the 10 s check; the cause is not established beyond this. The historical record keeps the prefix length only, not its bytes; byte equality is not claimed
